title: Boyd
author: Robert Coram
reason: Energy-maneuverability tradeoffs and decision feedback provide transferable payload. The new comment explicitly doubts some personal anecdotes; that supports the existing evidence and prose limits rather than a newly proven central factual failure.

title: The World is Flat
author: Thomas L. Friedman
reason: Retain the prior low-confidence no-veto decision and all ten attainments. The flattening metaphor is overbroad, but the account still explains outsourcing, communication and supply chains. Read as a 2005 argument, not a current forecast. No new evidence establishes a central failure serious enough to replace the prior judgment.

title: The Perfectionists
author: Simon Winchester
reason: Measurement and tolerances explain important enabling constraints. The prior unresolved technical-error leads do not establish a serious central failure; no veto.

title: Liftoff
author: Eric Berger
reason: Retain the prior eligibility, no-veto finding and all ten attainments after reviewing the excerpt and specialist reception recorded in the prior analysis. Failure diagnosis, testing and launch logistics remain central. The source adds no independent quality evidence. Retain 2008 as the first successful Falcon 1 launch endpoint.

title: The Theory That Would Not Die
author: Sharon Bertsch McGrayne

title: Elon Musk
author: Walter Isaacson
reason: A technology-founder biography with extensive access, but the subject’s personal and media presence is unusually central, so T11 applies. Iteration, manufacturing and organizational control supply payload. A documented Starlink correction lowers confidence; one corrected episode does not establish failure of the whole central account.

title: Civilian Warriors
author: Erik Prince
reason: A participant defense and history of Blackwater. Procurement, contracting and organizational constraints provide some payload. Self-exculpatory testimony substantially limits E/P; no independently established central factual failure is asserted here.

title: Welcome to Your Brain
author: Sandra Aamodt; Sam Wang
reason: A general brain-science explanation debunking myths. Advice is incidental to the explanatory overview, not a technical cognitive-training program.

title: Irresistible
author: Adam Alter
reason: A general account of behavioral addiction and attention technology. Reward schedules and product incentives provide transferable mechanisms. Practical suggestions are secondary to the explanatory narrative. Broad use of the addiction category limits confidence; it is not by itself proof of a serious central failure.

title: End Times
author: Peter Turchin
reason: A broad structural-demographic hypothesis, not a specialist modeling textbook. Forecast limitations reduce evidence and precision. They do not by themselves establish a serious central V1 or V4 failure.

title: Persepolis (complete memoir)
author: Marjane Satrapi
reason: A nonfiction graphic memoir of life under political and religious coercion, rather than a fabricated graphic novel. The original narrative is not converted into a manifesto by later promotional descriptions.

title: Takedown
author: Tsutomu Shimomura; John Markoff
reason: The contemporary review identifies self-promotion and conflicted framing. Lower E, D and P accordingly; documented tracing mechanisms retain value, and the evidence does not show that the whole technical account depends on a proven fabrication.

title: Dark Hero of the Information Age
author: Flo Conway; Jim Siegelman
reason: Useful history of Wiener and cybernetics, but the family-centered explanation of lost scientific influence needs caution. Specialist criticism lowers confidence; a serious central factual failure is not established by the inspected material.

title: The Ancient Engineers
author: L. Sprague de Camp
reason: Material constraints and accumulated invention offer useful historical payload. The older popular synthesis needs caution about superseded details; no specific serious central failure established.

title: Lost Continents
author: L. Sprague de Camp
reason: Tracing how conjectures acquire apparent authority offers transferable epistemic value. Read as a historical critical account, with dated scientific details; no serious central epistemic failure is established by age alone.

title: Darwin's Dangerous Idea
author: Daniel C. Dennett
reason: Retain with reduced evidence confidence for contested extensions of adaptationist reasoning. Gould's criticism and Dennett's reply establish a serious dispute, but the inspected exchange does not establish a decisive V1 or V2 failure. Philosophical centrality receives T12.

title: Atomic Accidents
author: James Mahaffey
reason: No serious veto established. Failure analysis has strong payload; the author’s stated support for nuclear energy requires attention to case selection but does not itself establish ideological capture.

title: The Man Who Ate His Boots
author: Anthony Brandt
reason: No serious veto established. Failed learning and resource constraints provide transferable lessons. The inspected review identifies peripheral factual mistakes, which lower precision without establishing central V1 failure.

title: Science in Action
author: Bruno Latour
reason: Networks of instruments, documents and allies offer useful institutional perspective. Strong constructionist formulations require qualification; no specific central factual failure was established in this bounded review.

title: Big Magic
author: Elizabeth Gilbert
reason: Personal conduct, coping, fulfillment, relationships or self-development is a central practical purpose. Apply V7’s life-support branch, even when philosophy, psychology or professional experience supplies the framework.

title: Start With Why
author: Simon Sinek
reason: The central argument about purpose and communication is developed through business narratives. It is no longer hard-excluded merely as a leadership framework. The former broad skill-development/expert-audience exclusion is not retained. H1 passes; no serious V1–V5 failure is established by the cited evidence.

title: The Smartest Investment Book You'll Ever Read
author: Daniel R. Solin
reason: The central argument for simple low-cost investing is general explanatory finance. It is not chiefly a technical execution or system-operation manual. The former broad skill-development/expert-audience exclusion is not retained. H1 passes; no serious V1–V5 failure is established by the cited evidence.

title: Area 51: An Uncensored History of America's Top Secret Military Base
author: Annie Jacobsen
reason: Retain V1: the sensational Roswell explanation involving Soviet human experimentation depends on an uncorroborated account, while the cited aerospace historian identifies concrete technical errors. Genuine secrecy history does not repair the material inferential failure in a central advertised revelation.

title: Dreamstate
author: Jed McKenna
reason: Retain V5: the work presents spiritual realization and the unreality of ordinary experience as its guiding authoritative truth. The finding concerns nondual doctrine, not the sensational subtitle or a supposed factual conspiracy claim.

title: Open Veins of Latin America
author: Eduardo Galeano
reason: Lift V5: anti-imperialist history and emancipation advocacy are allowed. The dependency framework remains oversimplified, but the prior evidence did not establish a serious central factual failure or asymmetric allegiance beyond that score limitation.

title: Operation Paperclip
author: Annie Jacobsen
reason: Retain V1: Neufeld documents recurring technical and institutional errors and invented dramatic detail, including treating V1 and V2 as successive versions. Those failures affect the central technological narrative, independently of the moral position.

title: Science at the Crossroads
author: Herbert Dingle
reason: Retain V1 at high confidence: the claimed relativistic contradiction compares clock rates defined with different event pairs and simultaneity conventions. A sustained expert argument passes the reference gate but does not validate that error.

title: The Decline of the West
author: Oswald Spengler
reason: Retain V1 at moderate confidence: the primary text treats civilizational analogy as historical necessity, including inevitable Caesarism and unavoidable imperialism. This is a central inferential failure, not a veto on pessimism or comparative history. The broader work contains observations and political contingencies, which remain credited but do not establish the asserted necessary sequence.

title: Billion Dollar Whale
author: Tom Wright and Bradley Hope
reason: Documents and reporting explain failures of financial and political checks beyond the central personality.

title: Catching Fire
author: Richard Wrangham
reason: The cooking hypothesis provides an explicit energetic mechanism. Uncertain timing and evolutionary inference reduce confidence without establishing central failure.

title: Makers: The New Industrial Revolution
author: Chris Anderson
reason: Digital design, desktop fabrication and open collaboration connect production scale to new business models.

title: Fab: From Personal Computers to Personal Fabrication
author: Neil Gershenfeld
reason: Digital fabrication connects tools, local production and the distribution of design capability.

title: Cambodia’s Curse
author: Joel Brinkley
reason: The specialist Contemporary Southeast Asia review identifies concrete errors and central unsupported inference from an allegedly unchanging national culture to contemporary failure, while acknowledging valuable reporting in much of the book.

title: Extraordinary Popular Delusions and the Madness of Crowds
author: Charles Mackay
reason: The influential tulipmania case materially supports the crowd-irrationality account using propagated anecdotes and claims of universal participation and broad ruin contradicted by archival scholarship. This is a central evidential failure, not an assertion that every historical essay is false.

title: Czechoslovakia: The State That Failed
author: Mary Heimann
reason: Central causal narrative overextends an undefined nationalist explanation across distinct regimes and underweights contrary democratic evidence, corroborated by two specialist critiques; revisionist conclusions alone are not the veto.

title: The Examined Life: How We Lose and Find Ourselves
author: Stephen Grosz

title: Random Reminiscences of Men and Events
author: John D. Rockefeller
